name: Pragmatic Reference Across Competitor Structures
summary: Listener referent choice and prior elicitation across multi-object scenes with varying competitor similarity, singleton status, and feature overlap.

charter.question: How do listeners combine recursive pragmatic inference, competitor confusion penalties, and perceptual singleton/isolation priors when interpreting referring expressions across diverse scene geometries?

instructions.welcome: Welcome! In this short study you will look at sets of friendly robots and figure out which robot a speaker is talking about.
instructions.task: On each screen you will see several robots. A speaker who can see the same robots says a single word that describes a part of the robot they mean (or on some screens, you will simply pick which robot stands out before hearing a word). Click the robot you think the speaker means.

comprehension_checks.question: What is your task when the speaker says a word?
options: Click the robot you think the speaker is referring to.
Click every robot that does not have that part.
Type a new name for the robot.

comprehension_checks.question: Can the speaker see the same robots on the screen that you see?
options: Yes, the speaker sees the exact same group of robots.
No, the speaker cannot see any of the robots.
The speaker only sees one robot.
